title: Determining grasp selection from arm trajectories via deep learning to enable functional hand movement in tetraplegia.
summary: The primary report compares DTW and LSTM trajectory classifiers in two cervical-SCI participants and combines real-time classification with neuromuscular stimulation to produce functional grasping.
ai_technology: Deep learning classifies arm trajectories and grasp intent from inertial-sensor time series.
organization: Feinstein Institutes for Medical Research at Northwell Health; Institute for Bioelectronic Medicine

evidence.tested: LSTM reached mean offline accuracy of 99%; DTW enabled online stimulation-controlled grasping in participants.
evidence.unknown: The study provides participant-level offline and online proof-of-concept validation, with limitations stated.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning classifies arm trajectories and grasp intent from inertial-sensor time series.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
